title: How cheap AI is made: distillation
label: AI EXPLAINED

yt.title: Under 30 minutes, under ₹5,000
notes: Under 30 minutes, under ₹5,000 (~$50) of rented GPUs
Beat OpenAI's o1-preview on competition maths (researchers' report)
Its teacher: a smarter AI. That's distillation

lines.text: Under thirty minutes. Under five thousand rupees. [1] That's what it took to make an existing AI beat an OpenAI reasoning model at maths, its researchers say. [2] Its teacher? [3] A smarter AI. This is called distillation.
lines.tts: Under thirty minutes. Under five thousand rupees. That's what it took to make an existing AI beat an Open AI reasoning model at maths, its researchers say. Its teacher? A smarter AI. This is called distillation.

yt.title: A big AI teaches a small one
notes: Teacher: big, slow, expensive
Student: small and fast

lines.text: The idea: [1] a big, slow, expensive AI [2] teaches a small, fast one.

yt.title: More than the final answer
notes: An answer key only says 'cat'
The teacher gives 90% cat, 9% tiger, 1% car
Chatbots do this with words: how the teacher weighs every next word

lines.text: An answer key just says 'cat'. [1] A teacher AI shows how much it looks like each option: [2] ninety percent cat, nine percent tiger, one percent car. [3] Those small numbers are hidden lessons. [4] Chatbots learn the same way, with words: the student copies how the teacher weighs every next word.
lines.tts: An answer key just says: cat. A teacher AI shows how much it looks like each option: ninety percent cat, nine percent tiger, one percent car. Those small numbers are hidden lessons. Chat bots learn the same way, with words: the student copies how the teacher weighs every next word.

yt.title: 97% of the score, much faster
notes: DistilBERT (2019): kept 97% of the teacher's score
40% smaller, 60% faster
Google: Gemini 1.5 Flash learned from 1.5 Pro (2024)

lines.text: It works. [1] One famous student kept ninety-seven percent of its teacher's score, [2] while being forty percent smaller and sixty percent faster. [3] And Google said its Gemini Flash learned from the bigger Pro this way.
lines.tts: It works. One famous student kept ninety-seven percent of its teacher's score, while being forty percent smaller and sixty percent faster. And Google said its Jemini Flash learned from the bigger Pro this way.

yt.title: 1,000 worked solutions
notes: An already-trained open model + 1,000 step-by-step solutions
Under 30 minutes on rented GPUs
Under ₹5,000 (s1, Stanford/UW/Ai2, 2025)

lines.text: And that maths model? [1] Researchers gave an already-trained open model one thousand worked solutions from a smarter AI. [2] Under thirty minutes of rented chips, [3] under five thousand rupees.
lines.tts: So, that maths model? Researchers gave an already-trained open model one thousand worked solutions from a smarter AI. Under thirty minutes of rented chips, under five thousand rupees.

yt.title: Copied mistakes, and the rules
notes: The student copies the teacher's mistakes
Big AI companies' terms ban training a rival on their answers

lines.text: The catch: [1] the student copies its teacher's mistakes too. [2] And most big AI companies' terms ban using their answers to build a rival.

yt.title: Mini/Flash first, Pro when it slips
notes: Emails, summaries, extracting data: start with mini or flash
Multi-step reasoning, or it keeps slipping: switch to Pro
Test on 20 real examples first

lines.text: So which do you use? [1] Emails, summaries, pulling out data: start with mini or flash. Faster, and cheaper if you pay. [2] Multi-step reasoning, or it keeps slipping? Switch to Pro. [3] And test on twenty real examples first.
